misconceptions: b  # sign error: derivative of cos x taken as +sin x
c  # derivative of a product taken as the product of the derivatives
d  # cos x treated as a constant (second product-rule term dropped)

review.notes: Author-written, modelled on the 3.5 product-rule-with-trig exercises (e.g. 177, 181). Product rule: (x^2)'cos x + x^2 (cos x)' = 2x cos x - x^2 sin x, so a. Distractors: b flips the sign of (cos x)'; c is (x^2)'(cos x)' = -2x sin x; d drops the x^2 (cos x)' term. Each is genuinely wrong, e.g. at x = pi/2: y' = -pi^2/4, b = +pi^2/4, c = -pi, d = 0. SymPy confirmed a equals y' and b, c, d do not. 2026-10-19: LaTeX parenthesized for R22; meaning unchanged (proved equal to the previous compiled answer).

d  # derivative of sin taken as sin

review.notes: Author-written, modelled on the 3.6 chain-rule exercises (e.g. 217, 235). Chain rule: cos(x^2) * 2x, so a. Each distractor is genuinely wrong, e.g. at x = 1: y' = 2cos 1 = 1.0806; b = cos 1 = 0.5403; c = cos 2 = -0.4161; d = 2 sin 1 = 1.6829.

15x^2-x  # differentiated only the cubic term

32x^4+18x^2  # exponent not lowered

problems.statement_html: Find <math-field read-only>f'(x)</math-field> for <math-field read-only>f(x) = 8x^4 + 9x^2 - 1</math-field>.

misconceptions: 270x^4+39  # differentiated 39x/(x+1) as 39 instead of using the quotient rule

review.notes: Expand first: f(x) = 54x^5 + 39x/(x+1). Power rule: 270x^4. Quotient rule: 39[(x+1) - x]/(x+1)^2 = 39/(x+1)^2. So f'(x) = 270x^4 + 39/(x+1)^2, matching the OpenStax answer key for 111. Domain: undefined only at x = -1, so R minus {-1}. Cross-checked with a throwaway SymPy diff/simplify.

problems.statement_html: Find <math-field read-only>f'(x)</math-field> for <math-field read-only>f(x) = 3x\left(18x^4 + \frac{13}{x+1}\right)</math-field>.

misconceptions: \frac{5}{x^2}  # sign error: derivative of 1/x taken as +1/x^2
2x\left(-\frac{4}{x^3}-\frac{15}{x^4}\right)  # product of the derivatives

review.notes: Group 106-117 instruction: find f'(x). Expand: f(x) = 2 + 5/x, so f'(x) = -5/x^2, matching the OpenStax answer key for 113 (-5/x^2). Domain: f is undefined at x = 0, so R minus {0}.

problems.statement_html: Find <math-field read-only>f'(x)</math-field> for <math-field read-only>f(x) = x^2\left(\frac{2}{x^2} + \frac{5}{x^3}\right)</math-field>.

review.notes: Rewrite f(x) = 4x - 2x^(-1) + x^(-2); power rule gives f'(x) = 4 + 2x^(-2) - 2x^(-3) = 4 + 2/x^2 - 2/x^3. The OpenStax key gives (4x^4 + 2x^2 - 2x)/x^4, the same function (divide through by x^4). Domain: undefined only at x = 0, so R minus {0}. Cross-checked with a throwaway SymPy diff/simplify against both forms.

problems.statement_html: Find <math-field read-only>f'(x)</math-field> for <math-field read-only>f(x) = \frac{4x^3 - 2x + 1}{x^2}</math-field>.

misconceptions: -7x+4  # used f(-1) = 4 as the y-intercept
-7x  # left out the point entirely

review.notes: f(-1) = -2 + 4 + 5 - 3 = 4. f'(x) = 6x^2 + 8x - 5, so f'(-1) = 6 - 8 - 5 = -7. y - 4 = -7(x + 1) gives y = -7x - 3, matching the OpenStax answer key for 137. The graded answer is the right-hand side -7x - 3 (instruction added). Domain: all reals.

misconceptions: \frac{9}{11}  # reported the position s(3) instead of the velocity
\frac{6}{11}  # quotient rule numerator terms subtracted the wrong way

review.notes: The [T] (technology) tag is dropped. Quotient rule: s'(t) = [2t(t^2+2) - t^2(2t)]/(t^2+2)^2 = 4t/(t^2+2)^2. s'(3) = 12/121 = 0.099173..., 0.0992 to 4 decimals, matching the OpenStax answer key for 145 (12/121 or 0.0992 ft/s). R24 wording added: exact or 4 decimal places.

Determine the velocity of the herring, in ft/s, when it has traveled 3 seconds. Give an exact answer or round to 4 decimal places.

misconceptions: (1-\sin(x))^2+(x+\cos(x))\cos(x)  # sign error: derivative of -sin x taken as +cos x

review.notes: Product rule with u = x + cos x, v = 1 - sin x: u' = 1 - sin x, v' = -cos x. dy/dx = (1 - sin x)(1 - sin x) + (x + cos x)(-cos x) = (1 - sin x)^2 - cos x (x + cos x), matching the OpenStax answer key for 181. Domain: all reals (only sin, cos and polynomials). Cross-checked with a throwaway SymPy diff/simplify. LaTeX puts the cos x factor last: Compute Engine parses \cos x\,(x+\cos x) as cos(x(x + cos x)). 2026-10-19: LaTeX parenthesized for R22; meaning unchanged (proved equal to the previous compiled answer).

problems.statement_html: Find <math-field read-only>\frac{dy}{dx}</math-field> for <math-field read-only>y = (x + \cos x)(1 - \sin x)</math-field>.

misconceptions: x  # sign error: derivative of -sin x taken as +cos x
-1  # slope only, no line

review.notes: Group 185-190 instruction: tangent line at the indicated x. f(0) = 0, f'(x) = -cos x, f'(0) = -1, so y = -x, matching the OpenStax answer key for 185. Graded answer is the right-hand side (instruction added). Domain: all reals.

review.notes: Group 185-190 instruction. f(3pi/2) = 1 + 0 = 1; f'(x) = -sin x, f'(3pi/2) = -(-1) = 1. y - 1 = x - 3pi/2 gives y = x + 1 - 3pi/2 = x + (2 - 3pi)/2, matching the OpenStax answer key for 187. Domain: all reals.

misconceptions: -\sin\left(-\frac{x}{8}\right)  # missing du/dx = -1/8
\frac{1}{8}\sin\left(\frac{x}{8}\right)  # sign error in the inner derivative

review.notes: Group 214-219 instruction: find dy/dx with Leibniz notation. dy/du = -sin u, du/dx = -1/8, so dy/dx = -sin(-x/8) * (-1/8), matching the OpenStax answer key for 217. Replaces a 235 draft (y = sin(cos 7x)): its correct answer proves instantly but wrong answers time out in the verifier, so students would see "could not check" instead of "not quite".

review.notes: Exercise 221 also asks to decompose (part a: u = 3x^2 + 1, y = u^3); only part b (dy/dx) is graded here. review.notes: Exercise 253 has parts a (velocity), b (acceleration) and c (speeding up or slowing down); only part a is graded here. v(t) = s'(t) = 100 * (-2)(t+1)^(-3) * 1 = -200/(t+1)^3. v(6) = -200/7^3 = -200/343 = -0.58309... m/s (-0.583 to 3 decimals), matching the OpenStax answer key for 253a.
